teaser: RiskMandate's go-to-market plan: one workflow from an existing business rule to evidence that still holds after a change, starting with our own inbox.
core_idea: RiskMandate's go-to-market plan is to deliver one chain end to end, existing requirement, approved agent delegation, implemented control, observed result and evidence valid after change, packaged as a six-part delegation record, with human rules translated through an explicit approval, baselines never learned from behaviour, three stages that test value, maintenance and repeatability, and a first pilot on its own inbox, where Gmail cannot enforce draft-but-never-send.

nodes.summary: Six parts a customer can act on.

nodes.label: A people rule is not a delegation

quotes.text: existing requirement → approved agent delegation → implemented control → observed result → evidence that remains valid after change
A model can propose an interpretation; it must not quietly inherit the authority of the original policy.
there is no permission that lets an agent draft without also letting it send

figures.caption: The chain to deliver once, end to end: an existing requirement, an approved delegation, an implemented control, an observed result, and evidence that still holds after a change.

The delegation record in six parts, business requirement, agent delegation, control mapping, evidence, remaining gaps and change conditions, filled in for pilot zero, our own inbox, as the plan stands; nothing in it has been tested yet.

A rule for people is not yet a delegation to an agent: refunds up to £100, the amount, one refund, a team lead's approval, eligibility and the process approval, each with the question an agent deployment must also answer.

Three stages: immediate value, fix one mismatch and show it from the protected system; maintenance value, make a controlled change and show what it invalidates; repeatability, a related workflow or a second customer, measuring what was reused.
